output.summary: The yield fall is real (stable CMM gauge R&R, program and criteria), so H5 holds. The new-operator cohort is exonerated: their reject rates match experienced operators, and yield was already falling before they ran alone. Three candidate causes remain confounded: deferred spindle service (runout and vibration rising, L3-02 and L3-05 worst), the Corvane bar change (higher hardness spread, but lots ran in sequence with time), and 12-hour fatigue. Scrap tag times are batch-written, so the evidence for fatigue is an artifact. Reverting shifts or cancelling Corvane now would be premature, and sampling inspection or punishing operators would be harmful. The staggered service plus Tamsworth trial and cycle-counter matching is the discriminating next step. The Line 6 Corvane results (X3) are the best single request.
